I use a credit card - only have one - for practically everything - other than utility bills and such that I pay via my credit union online bill paying service; I always pay off the balance in full, so I don't pay any interest; I use it for a number of reasons (in no particular order):

It's convenient, it provides some level of protection when doing purchases - better than what a debit card would (online in particular, but it got me out of some scammy transactions once or twice), some cards provide insurance / extended warranty on some purchases (mine does, got me a new laptop once when its motherboard fried a week or so past its manufacturer warranty...), when travelling abroad the exchange rate can be quite favorable, and there is some reward / cash back feature that gives me a small discounts on all my purchases (not enough in itself to chose said card over others but it's a nice touch); moreover, it provides some easy kind of record keeping - all in one place - of all my purchases for budgeting purposes. Oh, and it makes it easy to do things like purchasing plane tickets, booking hotel rooms and renting cars which would be a royal pain without a credit card.

I.e., not one of these reasons would in itself justify getting a credit card, but put all together it makes for a pretty compelling argument IMHO.
